page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.8-32 is a flexible virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7742 processor operating at a base clock frequency of 2.25 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, this configuration supplies 8 physical CPU cores mapped across 16 dedicated virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Network access includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The configuration does not include local NVMe or solid-state storage, necessitating the attachment of remote block volumes for persistent disk storage, nor does it include hardware GPU accelerators.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio characterizes this flexible profile as a compute-oriented deployment within the standard family. Because CPU allocations are dedicated rather than shared or burstable, compute performance remains predictable across persistent execution cycles. Without integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, the resource footprint emphasizes central processor capacity relative to memory footprint, offering a cost-efficient deployment profile for organizations seeking AMD multi-core processing without paying for excess memory or local scratch disks.

This instance profile fits workloads that require continuous parallel processing capacity with moderate memory footprints. Relevant use cases include web application hosting, build systems, continuous integration pipelines, batch data transformations, and containerized microservices that depend on network-attached storage architectures.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.8-32 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7742 processor running at 2.25 GHz. The configuration allocates 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per thread. The server does not bundle local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached block volumes for data persistence. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provided for external network access. Due to its dedicated CPU resource model and lean memory footprint, this instance provides predictable compute capacity without the overhead of unused RAM or bundled local storage. VM.Standard.E3.Flex.8-32 is suited for horizontally scalable compute tasks, continuous integration workers, web servers, and distributed batch processing.
